findings.title: caught-up reports yes/no when the wanted range has a start but no known end
findings.description: `wanted` is only set when both `wanted_start` and `wanted_end` exist (lines 186–193). But line 217 passes `wanted=wanted_start is not None` to `caught_up`. For a product with a tier, no `entry.end`, and no observed edge, `_scope` returns only the sessions that held units touch. `caught_up` then evaluates just those, so it can print `caught up: yes` while sessions in the wanted range are never checked, including gaps before the first held day. The slice 225 doc says a product without a wanted range is "n/a", and the `caught_up` docstring (`tick_status.py:152-156`) says the same. The integration test only exercises the tier-`None` ES entry (`universe.py:46`), so this path has no coverage. Fix: pass `wanted=wanted is not None`, and add a test with a tier set and no edge.

findings.title: `calendar_sessions` copies the error translation from `product_session_days`
findings.description: `calendar_sessions` (lines 63–75) repeats `product_session_days` (`tick_calendar.py:67-81`) almost line for line. Both open a `TradingCalendar`, catch `(psycopg.OperationalError, CalendarNotFoundError)` and `OutOfPopulatedRangeError`, re-raise each as `TickCalendarError` with the same messages, and close in `finally`. That mapping decides the exit code through `exit_code_for`, so it should exist once. Fix: move a blocking `sessions_between` wrapper into `tick_calendar.py` and have both callers use it.

findings.title: `status_reads` repeats the unit/request join and breaks the manifest modules' single-home rule
findings.description: `_UNITS` repeats `UNIT_FROM` from `manifest_reads.py:90`. That join is also written inline in `manifest_reads.py` at lines 167–170 and 199–201. The docstring at `manifest_reads.py:5-6` says every SQL statement on `tick_request` and `tick_archive_unit` lives in one of three modules (`manifest_reads`, `manifest_request_reads`, `manifest_repo`). `status_reads.py` is a fourth home. Fix: import `UNIT_FROM`, or move the status SQL into one of those three modules.

findings.title: `raw_counts` joins on a range predicate; the cost is unmeasured
findings.description: `raw_counts` joins `tick_trade` to `unnest(...)` on `t.ts_event BETWEEN s.open_ns AND s.close_ns`. A range predicate cannot drive a hash or merge join, so Postgres will likely run a nested loop that compares each tick row in the range against every session in the array. The cost scales as rows × sessions. The `WHERE` bound limits the rows scanned, but not the per-row work. I did not measure this. The project's SQL rules require `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` for tuning, so run it on a realistic multi-month range before relying on `coverage`. A per-session `LATERAL` count over `tick_trade` is one alternative to benchmark.

findings.title: Exit 4 covers more than the epilog says, and the calendar-outage path is untested
findings.description:
- `calendar_sessions` converts `OutOfPopulatedRangeError` into `TickCalendarError`, and `exit_code_for` maps that to `EXIT_STORAGE` (`tick_exit.py:54-57`). A `--start` or `--end` outside the calendar's populated span therefore exits 4 ("storage"). `READ_EPILOG` (`tick_store_cmds.py:37-42`) lists exit 1 for input errors and exit 4 only for an unreachable database, so this case matches neither.
- `READ_EPILOG` promises exit 4 when the calendar database is unreachable. `calendar_sessions` catches only `psycopg.OperationalError` and `CalendarNotFoundError`. `TradingCalendar.__init__` creates `ConnectionPool(..., open=True)` (`trading_calendar.py:154`), so connection failures surface later, in `_ensure_loaded` (line 194). I could not confirm which exception class the pool raises. No test covers an unreachable calendar on `status` or `coverage`; `test_tick_status_cli.py:147` only covers the tick database.

Fix: decide whether an out-of-range input is preflight (exit 1), then add a test with an unreachable calendar URL that asserts the code the epilog states.

findings.title: Import-time `assert` guards the status bucket table
findings.description: The check that `_BUCKET_ROWS` covers every `TickSessionStatus` is an `assert` at import. Under `python -O` it disappears, and a new status would silently drop out of the report. `tick_exit.py:32` uses the same pattern, so this follows repo convention. A `raise` at import, or a unit test, would hold under `-O` as well.

findings.title: `_product_lines` is about 54 lines and mutates its last line
findings.description: Lines 57–110 run about 54 lines, past the ~50-line guideline. Line 80 (`lines[-1] += ...`) appends "(degraded N)" to whichever line was added last. That is correct only by construction. Splitting the edge, bucket, and contract sections into helpers would make it explicit.

findings.title: `age()` renders negative durations and has no unit test
findings.description: If `observed_at` is ahead of the host clock, `edge_age_seconds` is negative. `age(-3600)` evaluates to `"-1d 23h"`. No test imports `tick_status_render` (a grep of `test/` finds nothing), so this branch and the other `age` branches are untested. Clamp at zero, or print an explicit clock-skew message.

findings.title: Connection and status fields are loosely typed where types exist
findings.description: `_read` and the `read` closure in `tick_coverage` (`tick_store_cmds.py:228`) take `conn: Any`, but `Conn` is defined at `manifest_reads.py:29`. `ProductStatus.buckets` (`tick_status_build.py:113`) is `dict[str, int]` keyed by `TickSessionStatus` values, and `stype_in` (line 103) is `str` where `SType` exists. `CoverageSession.status` (`tick_coverage.py:45`) is `str` where `TickSessionStatus` exists.

findings.title: Test helper duplicates the settings/logging patch from two other test files
findings.description: `_app_patches` (lines 45–56) is the same two-patch context manager as the inline `no_key` fixture in `test_tick_ingest_cli.py:47-56` and the `settings` fixture in `test_data_tick_ingest.py:75-86`, both of which this diff also edits. The `setup_logging` patch already appears at about 30 call sites in the repo, so the pattern predates this change, but this diff adds three more copies. A shared fixture in `test/conftest.py` or `tick_support` would hold it in one place.

findings.title: Render branches have no direct unit tests
findings.description: The no-edge line, holed sessions, the `caught up: n/a` line, empty contracts, and the all-instruments header are reached only through CLI integration tests. Several are not asserted at all. The renderer is pure, so parametrized unit tests over `ProductStatus` values would cover each branch cheaply.

findings.title: Status and coverage SQL binds all values as parameters
findings.description: Dataset, symbols, stype, tiers, session bounds, and dates all go through `%(name)s` or `%s` placeholders. The f-strings interpolate only module constants (`_UNITS`, `_SHAPE_WHERE`, `COVERAGE_PREDICATE`), so there is no injection path.

findings.title: New tests and code do not read a production database URL
findings.description: `test_a_coverage_mismatch_exits_3` issues a `DELETE` against `migrated_tick_db`. That fixture is built on `ephemeral_tick_db`, which creates its own database (`test/conftest.py:205, 313`). The `ingested` fixture removes `MT_TICK_*` and `DATABENTO*` variables before running. Neither the new tests nor the new source read a production URL variable.
